events.factual_description: Birdland Jazz Club presents Makoto Ozone Trio 'Remembering Kiyoshi Kitagawa' featuring Yasushi Nakamura on bass and Clarence Penn on drums from Tuesday, August 25 through Saturday, August 29, 2026. Tuesday through Thursday sets are at 7:00 PM and 9:30 PM; Friday and Saturday sets are at 8:30 PM and 10:30 PM. Birdland describes the engagement as a celebration of Ozone's late friend and bassist Kiyoshi Kitagawa. Ozone's official schedule independently confirms the August 25-29 Birdland run and billing. Kitagawa died on April 28, 2026. Ozone, Kitagawa and Penn formed Makoto Ozone's landmark trio in 1997; The Trio documents that original piano-bass-drums relationship. No additional guests or repertoire are announced on the official event page and none are inferred.

en.why_it_matters: This is more than a pianist dedicating a set to a late colleague. Kitagawa and Clarence Penn were the rhythm section of the trio Ozone formed in the late 1990s, and that band helped define a major chapter of his New York jazz life. With Penn back at the drums and Yasushi Nakamura now occupying the bass chair, the memorial has musical architecture as well as sentiment: the trio format itself carries the absence. Kitagawa died only four months ago, so the Birdland run is close enough to the loss that memory, continuity and the act of replacing a bassist without pretending to replace the person should all be audible in the music.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the remaining Birdland sets if New York is already in reach this week. The Japanese-New York lineage and the direct Ozone-Kitagawa-Penn history make this substantially more meaningful than a routine Ozone trio booking. Five nights and ten sets give enough access that I would not displace a genuinely singular premiere, farewell or one-night reunion elsewhere in the corridor solely to catch this run.

es.why_it_matters: Esto es bastante más que un pianista dedicándole un set a un colega que murió. Kitagawa y Clarence Penn fueron la sección rítmica del trío que Ozone armó a finales de los noventa, y esa banda definió una etapa importante de su vida jazzística en Nueva York. Con Penn de nuevo en la batería y Yasushi Nakamura ocupando ahora la silla del bajo, el homenaje tiene arquitectura musical además de carga afectiva: el propio formato de trío carga con la ausencia. Kitagawa murió hace apenas cuatro meses, así que esta residencia en Birdland ocurre lo bastante cerca de la pérdida como para que memoria, continuidad y la dificultad de sustituir un instrumento sin fingir que se sustituye a la persona puedan sentirse dentro de la música.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los sets restantes de Birdland si Nueva York está al alcance esta semana. El hilo Japón–Nueva York y la historia directa Ozone–Kitagawa–Penn vuelven esta residencia mucho más significativa que una fecha rutinaria del trío. Las cinco noches y diez funciones dan suficiente acceso para que no desplace únicamente por esto un estreno realmente singular, una despedida o una reunión de una sola noche en otro punto del corredor.
